To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
H. pylori RNA polymerases αCTD has an extended C‐terminal region and binds to NikR/DNA cooperatively.

H. pylori RNA polymerases αCTD has a conserved DNA binding surface but an additional amphipathically charged C‐terminal helix unique to ɑ‐proteobacterial RNA polymerases that may function in transcriptional regulation.

the αCTD from Helicobacter has a unique C‐terminal extension and cooperatively binds to the DNA‐binding protein NikR, suggesting that this domain is important in the regulation of transcription by NikR.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structural and functional characterization of the C‐terminal domain (CTD) of the α‐subunit of RNA polymerases from the ɛ‐class proteobacteria.
the structure of the C‐terminal domain (CTD) of the α subunits of RNA Polymerase (RNAP) from Helicobacter pyroli.
the structure, function, and evolution of αCTD, and how it may interact with other transcription factors in H. pylori.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the αCTD from Helicobacter is larger than those from other bacteria and contains an additional helix that may mediate protein‐protein interactions with transcription factors.
the αCTD of H. pylor i is similar to other αCTDs, but with some unique features.

αCTD is an essential component in all bacteria and that it is highly conserved in terms of its structure and function, but that it has evolved to adapt to the specific requirements of the transcriptional regulation of each organism.

αCTD of H. pylor i shows features unique to the ɛ‐Proteobacteria and that the C‐terminal domain is important for binding to NikR:DNAs and may be important for the recruitment of RNA Polymerase to promoters.
the αCTD of H. pylor i is similar to those of other bacteria but also shows unique features that are likely to be involved in its interaction with transcriptional regulators.

The main takeaway from our work is that
αCTDs of different bacteria are capable of binding DNA and proteins in different ways.
the αCTD of ɛ‐bacteria has an extra helix that is important to its stability and function.
the αCTDs of ɛ‐Proteobacteria, including H. pylori, are larger than those of other bacteria due to an extra amphipathic, C‐terminal helix, which is likely to mediate interactions with other proteins.
